title: Token-level latency SLI plus multi-region failover & load-shedding visualizations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Instrument token-level latency SLIs and assemble a set of dashboards that show golden signals (+ token breakdowns), multi-region failover behavior, circuit-breaker activations, and load-shedding events. This ticket covers metric naming, sampling approach, query shapes, Grafana/Datadog dashboards, alert thresholds, and runbook links for on-call.

Background: We currently track request-level P50/P95/P99 for generation requests, but lack visibility into per-token latency distributions, the distribution of token counts per request, and the runtime behaviors when circuit breakers or region-fallbacks occur. Engineers and SREs need signal fidelity to diagnose tail latency regressions introduced by kernel changes, KV cache regressions, or autoscaler churn.

Scope & acceptance criteria:
- Instrument metrics emitted by runtime and SDK: token_processing_time_ms (histogram), tokens_emitted, kv_cache_hit_ratio, circuit_breaker_activations, shed_requests_count, region_fallback_count. Metric names must be prefixed redwood.runtime.
- Add derived SLIs: token_latency_p50/p95/p99/p995 (based on token_processing_time_ms), request_latency_by_token_count (heatmap), percentage of responses where token latency P99 > 50ms.
- Build Grafana dashboard "Runtime Token SLOs & Failover" that includes: golden signals (latency, errors, saturation), token latency heatmap, KV cache hit trend, per-region capacity/utilization, circuit breaker timeline, and load-shed events overlay.
- Create Datadog monitors for token_latency_p99 and circuit_breaker_activations with burn-rate alerting and a recover-to-green policy.
- Document runbook steps (link below) for investigating token tail regressions and region-fallback incidents.
- End-to-end test: synthetic workload that exercises KV cache cold path and triggers circuit-breaker to validate metrics and dashboards before release.

Implementation notes:
- Sampling: emit histogram buckets on the runtime side at every token boundary to avoid approximation at the SDK. Use sketches only for long-term retention aggregates (daily rollups).
- Tags: attach model, model_version, region, deployment_tier, tenant (when available) to metrics for drill-down. Avoid high-cardinality tags for production retention metrics; use tenancy sampling for low-volume tenants.
- Correlation: include trace_id and request_id in metric logs to tie into distributed tracing (x-trace link header).
- Circuit breaker events should include reason and threshold metadata so dashboard can annotate root cause (e.g., high-pqueue-delay, backend-gpu-unhealthy).
- Backfill: provide a script to backfill token histogram aggregates from recent trace logs (see attachments).

Rollout plan:
1) Spike + instrumentation PR for runtime (small canary on dedicated capacity).
2) Validate metrics in staging Grafana.
3) Deploy to 10% of hosted capacity, run synthetic tests for 24h.
4) Full rollout with on-call watch and alerting.

Out-of-scope: UI changes in Redwood Console for now; this ticket focuses on underlying metrics and dashboards.

2025-03-02 - PR #4627 (runtime) opened: initial instrumentation. Notes: needs SDK tag propagation fix before metrics are useful for tenant-level breakdowns.
2025-03-03 - Design review: Decided to keep tenant tag optional at emission time and use sampled tenant_id tag with fallback to 'unknown' to control cardinality. Approved by Samir Chen (SRE).

2025-03-05 - Blocker: Datadog ingestion quota for high-cardinality histograms flagged. Working with infra to create a lower-cardinality pipeline and a separate high-cardinality trace-backed path for debugging.
2025-03-06 - PR feedback addressed: added kv_cache_hit_ratio metric and circuit_breaker_reason label. Preparing Grafana dashboard JSON for review.
